extracted.subtask_description: A multi-item Associated Press newspaper dispatch reporting wartime policies, government actions, and post-war planning (aviation program, asset-disposition formula, detentions, shipment rules). Intended as news for the general public and officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-war aviation objective — help post-war civilian/commercial aviation
rubrics_metrics.description: To help post-war efforts in connection with civilian and commercial aviation, including employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item #1 in a nine-point post-war aviation program; frames aviation planning as tied to post-war civilian/commercial recovery and jobs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-war aviation objective — keep U.S. dominance of airways (broad routes)
rubrics_metrics.description: To maintain dominance of this country of airways from the United States to South America, Africa and the Far Pacific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit policy objective in the nine-point program to preserve strategic commercial/transport routes and influence after the war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-war aviation objective — expand and develop foreign airways and commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: To expand and develop foreign airways and commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the nine-point program emphasizing overseas aviation infrastructure and commercial expansion as post-war goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-war aviation objective — protect rights in lend-lease airfields
rubrics_metrics.description: To protect this country's rights in airfields built with lend-lease money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms a policy priority to safeguard legal/operational claims in airfields funded or constructed under lend-lease arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-war aviation objective — keep airplane factories and pilots employed
rubrics_metrics.description: To keep airplane factories and pilots busy after the war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A post-war economic/industrial objective to maintain aviation-sector employment and production capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-war aviation objective — prepare for improved travel and commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: To prepare for improved, faster and cheaper travel and commerce in post-war days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic objective to encourage technological and commercial advances in post-war civilian air transport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-war aviation objective — safeguard U.S. defense through aviation production
rubrics_metrics.description: To safeguard defense of the United States by producing the ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the nine-point program tying post-war aviation planning to national defense preparedness (text truncated in source but presented as a defense-safeguarding goal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-war aviation objective — promote airmindedness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural/educational objective in the nine-point plan to foster public support and awareness of aviation's role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-war aviation objective — (assist post-war efforts generally)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Additional listed aim to help post-war efforts — e.g., providing a standing committee to handle air-transportation matters, employment, and coordination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program included institutional proposals such as creating committees to handle air transportation and to assist post-war coordination of civilian/commercial aviation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of immovable US defense assets in Canada — one-year release rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The formula decrees that all immovable assets of the United States are to be released within one year after the end of the war to the Canadian Government or the provincial Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-war liquidation rule reported to the House of Commons: immovable (fixed) U.S. defense projects in Canada must be transferred/released within one year of war-end to Canadian authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of movable US defense assets in Canada — removal or offer-for-sale within one year
rubrics_metrics.description: All movable assets must be removed from Canada within one year or offered for sale to the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If movable assets are not removed or sold to the Crown within one year, they must be offered for sale on the open market; if they cannot be sold, their disposition is to be referred to the permanent joint defense board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation mechanism for sale of US movable defense assets in Canada
rubrics_metrics.description: The price would be fixed by two appraisers, one chosen by each country, with power to select a third in case of dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the appraisal/valuation procedure for sales of U.S. movable defense assets left in Canada after the one-year period; includes bilateral appraiser selection and tie-breaker mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order for detention/presentation of Axis nationals (Chile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Those affected by the order had been instructed Jan. 26 to remain in their homes and to present themselves at police stations before midnight for detention; order affected Axis nationals and their legation staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governmental/security directive applied as reprisal/detention following diplomatic ruptures (example: Chile confining Japanese minister and staff; instruction to Axis nationals to report for detention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on hard-coal shipment restrictions (emergency lifting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions on the shipment of hard coal to States and to points in the United States west of Erie, Pa., previously imposed to concentrate shipments into eastern States, have been lifted as an emergency expedient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative policy change explained as a response to strikes and fuel shortages (used to ease critical situation created by the strike in the hard coal mines and shortage of fuel oil on the Atlantic seaboard).
